newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK February inflation seen lower.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK February inflation seen lower.

text.p: British underlying inflation probably dipped below 3.0 percent in February, its first dip below that level in five months, economists say.
With the strong pound continuing to impact retailers' margins, goods prices are set to bring the RPIX underlying rate down to the government's 2.5 percent target before the end of the year.
Economists polled by Reuters expect the February data, due at 0930 GMT on Thursday, to show the annual underlying inflation rate fell to 2.9 percent from 3.1 percent in January.
Retail prices are forecast to have risen 0.5 percent on the month versus an unchanged rate in January, while the year-on-year rate is expected to remain at 2.8 percent.
Jonathan Loynes, economist at HSBC Markets, said upward pressure would come from higher mortgage rates, but lower seasonal food prices would take some of the sting out of inflationary pressure.

Clothing and footwear may also have come back from their sharply discounted levels in January, analysts said, although any rebound was likely to be muted given the latest Confederation of British Industry (CBI) survey showing prices expectations on the soft side.

"The net effect is to push the headline rate up from 2.8 percent to 2.9 percent, but the underlying rate -- which escapes the impact from mortgages -- should tick down from 3.1 percent to 3.0 percent," said Loynes.
James McKay, economist at PaineWebber said February's data would bring the "elusive" 2.5 percent government target for underlying inflation into view.

He said the recent strength of sterling -- which has gained around 15 percent on a trade-weighted basis since last summer -- would limit any recovery in February clothing and household goods prices after January's sales.

But, forecasting a fall in the RPIX annual rate to 2.9 percent from 3.1 percent, McKay said: "The stubbornness of service sector prices suggests to us that the target will not be hit until the second half of this year."

While higher mortgage rates -- after the rise in UK base rates to 6.00 percent on October 30 last year -- are likely to add heat to the inflation picture, some analysts said the absence of a sharp step up in house prices last year would help maintain inflation below 3.0 percent.
Ciaran Barr, UK economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said this coupled with lower food inflation and a further drop in petrol prices would force a decline in headline inflation in February.
"With sterling still strong, lower goods inflation should push RPIX inflation towards towards the government's target by the summer," Barr said.
